full_judgment:
9. Mr. Alam submits that when there is no intention of the parties to rescind the earlier contract altogether there is no substitution of the original contract by a subsequent one, and the original contract remains in force and still remains enforceable. And that being the position in the present case, the subsequent contract with present respondent No.1 is not enforceable in view of section 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act. He further submits that the plea of the subsequent purchaser that he entered into an agreement in respect of the suit property without notice of previous contract for sale having not been proved by him, the appellant's suit for specific performance of contract, which is of earlier date, will not be defeated. Thus the trial court rightly found that the subsequent agreement with Mostafa Kamal has been made to frustrate the earlier agreement with the appellant and also that the subsequent suit instituted by Mostafa Kamal(respondent No.1) is also barred by limitation. Moreover, on the face of admitted fact that none of the plaintiff's vendors(the sellers) having challenged the said decree of the trial court, even the brother and sister who did not sign the agreement as alleged, though appeared in the suit, also having not challenge the decree in appeal the impugned judgment of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

 12. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent No.1 in both the appeals, submits that release of the suit land from mortgage by paying Tk. 12,50,000/- to the bank, was the major condition which the plaintiff-appellant was bound to perform under section 47 of the Contract Act, but he having failed to perform the same his right to claim specific performance has ceased on 15.2.1986 under section 54 of the Contract Act. He next submits that when the plaintiff-appellant found that the bank dues were much higher than Tk. 12,50,000/-, he could either pay the whole amount of dues and claim adjustment as well as specific performance of contract or could treat the contract voidable at his option. But he having not availed either of the two options, he cannot get any relief in this suit. He further submits that since the plaintiff-appellant did not pay the contractual money within the stipulated period of 15.2.1986, he cannot claim specific performance of contract. He next submits that time being the essence of contract by lapse of the stipulated time the contract stood frustrated and as such the plaintiff cannot seek any relief. He also submits that pursuant to the contract of the present respondent No.1 dated 19.10.1986 the bank duly delivered the title deeds to him as he paid off the bank dues and was authorised to take delivery thereof; so no separate letter of authority was necessary. Lastly, he submits that the cause of action of the present respondent No. l's suit (Title Suit No. 233 of 1994) accrued on 1.5.1990 so, his suit was not barred by limitation; hence, the High Court Division rightly decreed his suit which is liable to be upheld by this Division. 

 18. Defendant Nos. 5 though claimed that the contract ceased to exist on plaintiff's failure to pay the contractual amount within the stipulated time i.e. 15.2.1986, but from the discussion made above it is clear that the plaintiff was always ready to deposit the contractual amount but due to the huge bank liability which is much higher than what he was contractually liable to pay and the defendants' indolent and indifferent attitude to release the suit property from the bank made the plaintiff unable to perform his part of depositing the said amount. So, the contract of the plaintiff-appellant shall prevail over that of defendant No.9 respondent No. l. On the other hand pursuant to section 53B of the Transfer of Property Act during the existence of the agreement for sale of the suit property with plaintiff-appellant of earlier date the subsequent agreement with defendant No.9 (respondent No.1) is void as the same has no legal effect. Moreover, the defendant No.9 in his pleadings claimed that the cause of action of his suit arose on 20.12.1986 but he instituted his suit on 12.7.1990 which is more than three and half years after he got himself added as defendant No.9 in the plaintiff's suit No. 44 of 1987 (Other Class Suit No. 234 of 1994) which is beyond the three years period of limitation as prescribed in Article 113 of the Limitation Act. Thus the trial court rightly found the said suit barred by limitation. But the High Court Division without taking this aspect into consideration decreed the present respondent Nod's suit reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court which cannot be sustained in the eye of law.
